summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with HCV-related cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and a history of GAVE-related bleeding, was admitted for dyspnea on exertion and lightheadedness due to anemia. His hemoglobin had dropped to 7.5 g/dL, likely from ongoing upper gastrointestinal blood loss related to GAVE. He received two units of packed red blood cells in the emergency department with improvement in symptoms and a rise in hemoglobin to 9.3 g/dL. Cardiac and pulmonary evaluations were unremarkable, and his chronic right upper quadrant pain was attributed to known intestinal malrotation. His cirrhosis remained stable without signs of decompensation. He was discharged home in stable condition with continued management of his liver disease, GAVE prophylaxis, and instructions to follow up with his liver specialist.
